rv.q: Craig identifies a core of thuggery in Macbeth — he's a lunkish, perhaps even dimwitted soldier of fortune who quickly gets drunk on ambition and power.
Watching the production and often being very engaged, I kept thinking how much better this 'Macbeth' would be if staged in-the-round
This 'Macbeth' struck me as a bit bloodless.

"Truly, it is difficult to fathom what Gold has in mind. Sometimes, the entire production comes off as if it were being performed by a high school class of mixed talents, assigned to read 'Macbeth' by their popular English teacher.

When you consider what might have been—a Macbeth with awe-inspiring sets and transportive costumes, the full complement of Broadway tricks that make ordinary productions extraordinary—particularly with top notch talent like Craig and Negga leading the way, you can only think of the missed opportunity.
Why is the cast so unattractively dressed? Why does Lady Macbeth host a dinner for Duncan and his entourage in a gown seemingly borrowed from Gold Diggers of 1933?
I can't imagine what someone who's never seen or read the play could possibly get here, except an excuse to catch up on their sleep.
